rule: Evidence supports admission or prioritisation of mechanisms; it does not substitute for parameter estimation, time-respecting validation or causal identification.

sources.title: Interest Rate Pass-Through in Romania and Other Central European Economies
sources.finding: Romanian policy-to-market interest-rate pass-through is empirically present and became more pronounced over time.
sources.limitations: Historical sample; coefficients cannot be reused as current calibration parameters.

sources.title: Romania: Annex VI. Monetary Policy Transmission Mechanism
sources.finding: Interest-rate and exchange-rate channels were found to have the strongest effects on output in the reported VAR analysis.
sources.limitations: VAR evidence establishes dynamic association/shock responses under its identification assumptions, not a timeless structural coefficient.

sources.title: Occasional Paper 15/2015 — bank lending channel / prudential regulation
sources.finding: Romanian bank-level credit dynamics are linked to the policy rate, reserve requirements, real growth and bank characteristics including solvency and loan-to-deposit ratios.
sources.limitations: Bank-level specification does not directly identify a single aggregate credit equation.

sources.title: Exchange Rate Pass-Through in Romania
sources.finding: FX pass-through to Romanian producer and consumer prices was large and relatively fast in the 1997–2003 sample.
sources.limitations: Pre-inflation-targeting regime; historical magnitudes must not be used as current parameters.

sources.title: Romania: Selected Issues — exchange-rate pass-through after inflation targeting
sources.finding: Exchange-rate pass-through remained relevant but diminished after Romania adopted inflation targeting.
sources.limitations: Supports regime dependence; argues against hard-coding older coefficients.

sources.title: Romania: 2025 Article IV Consultation
sources.finding: Large fiscal deficits, rising debt and tighter financing conditions/higher sovereign yields are material current Romanian macro-financial features.
sources.limitations: Institutional assessment and descriptive evidence do not identify a stable sovereign-yield structural equation.

sources.title: Debt Sustainability Monitor 2025 — Romania
sources.finding: Romania had a 10-year sovereign spread versus the German Bund of 391 bps at end-2025 and high short-/medium-term fiscal sustainability risks.
sources.limitations: Point-in-time risk assessment; does not identify marginal causal effects of debt or deficit on spreads.

sources.title: Economic forecast for Romania
sources.finding: Fiscal consolidation and high inflation are expected to weigh on domestic consumption while EU-funded investment remains important; financing conditions matter for the recovery.
sources.limitations: Forecast narrative is not parameter identification and is not used as calibration data.

sources.title: Bank interest rates — new housing loans, Romania, RON
sources.role: observable lending-rate target for monetary pass-through

sources.title: Bank interest rates — new loans to corporations, Romania, RON
sources.role: observable corporate lending-rate target for monetary pass-through/investment candidate

sources.institution: Eurostat / Romanian National Institute of Statistics
sources.title: GDP and main components — quarterly data
sources.role: GDP, household consumption and gross fixed capital formation observables

sources.title: Convergence Report — Romania, June 2026
sources.finding: Romania remained under a managed-float exchange-rate regime; 2025 deficit and debt ratios and exchange-rate developments are documented.
sources.limitations: Regime/context evidence, not a structural FX reaction equation.
